Definition: from the same as (the first part of) G220 and G435; man-defender; Alexander, the name of three Israelites and one other man:--Alexander.
BiblicalUsage: Four men share the name, and the Bible keeps them apart by their deeds. One stands with the high priest's kindred against Peter and John; one is the son of Simon of Cyrene, who carried the cross; one is put forward by the Jews in the Ephesus riot and shouted down; and Alexander the coppersmith does Paul much evil, and Paul delivers him with Hymenaeus unto Satan, that they may learn not to blaspheme.
TheologicalSignificance: A shared name carries no lesson of its own. What it shows is the Bible's plain record of opposition, that the gospel met men who fought it with their hands, their words and their crowds, and Paul names them without flinching.
